evidence: src/application/use-cases/AssignTaskUseCase.ts: execute() coordinates tasks.findById, users.findById, task.assignTo, tasks.save and toTaskDto. This is application-layer orchestration.
The business rule is handed to the domain entity through task.assignTo(user.id). The use case does not implement it.
Persistence goes only through the TaskRepository and UserRepository interfaces, which are injected through the constructor. The file has no storage or transport code.
NotFoundError and UnknownAssigneeError are application-level errors that report missing entities.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: AssignTaskUseCase is a typical application-layer use case. It coordinates the work: it loads the task and the user through domain repository interfaces and turns missing entities into application errors. It hands the assignment rule to the domain entity (task.assignTo), saves the result through the repository abstraction and maps the entity to a DTO. The file has no persistence code such as SQL or ORM calls, no transport or framework logic such as HTTP or request objects, and no business invariants of its own. The checks for a missing task or user are use-case preconditions, not domain rules, so they fit the application layer.
